title: Qumran aqueduct outlet
author: SuperJew
viewpoint: Close view of the aqueduct exit into a cistern at Qumran; precise camera coordinates are not supplied by the source.
alt: Close photograph of a small aqueduct opening beneath rough stone masonry, with a shallow curved plastered lip leading out into a cistern.
caption: An actual surviving waterwork at Qumran: the source identifies this as an aqueduct exit into a cistern. This is a close-up photograph, not a panorama or 360-degree capture. It does not show the upstream intake, dam, full channel, or an identified Copper Scroll hiding place.

highlights.label: Aqueduct outlet
highlights.note: Entry 21 describes the head of a conduit at Sekakah. This visible aqueduct exit illustrates Qumran’s surviving water system; the upstream intake named in the proposed reading is not shown or identified here.

highlights.label: Plastered outlet lip
highlights.note: A shallow curved plastered surface survives below the opening. Its visible form can be examined; the photograph cannot establish an ancient measured distance, depth, concealed cavity, or cache.

title: Jebel Qarantal escarpment from Jericho
author: Tango7174
viewpoint: Source camera coordinates: 31.874000, 35.433500; a view from the Jericho area toward the Mount of Temptation.
alt: Wide photograph of the Mount of Temptation's rocky escarpment above cultivated fields and scattered buildings near Jericho; cliffside buildings appear along the left slope.
caption: A wide ground-level photograph of the Mount of Temptation, commonly called Jebel Qarantal, from the Jericho area. The mountain and escarpment provide landscape context for the atlas's Doq candidate. The image does not establish the exact position of ancient Doq or any Copper Scroll cache.

highlights.label: Rocky escarpment
highlights.note: The exposed rocky mountain face is visible. This is broad terrain context only: neither a particular rock-cut chamber nor a named treasure landmark can be identified from this photograph.

highlights.label: Summit ridge
highlights.note: Entry 31 may refer to a fortress at Doq. This ridge gives the summit candidate its landscape setting. The photograph does not resolve the alternative reading, a drying floor, or identify the specified corner.

title: Wadi Qelt canyon near Choziba
author: Joel יוֹאֵל
viewpoint: Source camera coordinates: 31.842638, 35.413656; the canyon in the area of Saint George of Koziba/Choziba.
alt: Long stitched photograph of Wadi Qelt's dry canyon, layered cliff faces, narrow valley bed, and green patches along the slopes, beneath a visibly curved horizon.
caption: A stitched panorama of the canyon in the area of Choziba, photographed in 2007. Its edges are not a verified 360-degree seam. The highlighted terrain is landscape context; the monastery and a particular ancient aqueduct or treasure landmark are not confidently identifiable in this image.

highlights.label: Layered canyon wall
highlights.note: Entry 32 describes a water outlet and retaining wall at Koziba. The canyon setting can be examined here, but the visible ledges do not identify that outlet, wall, or a particular ancient conduit.

highlights.label: Dry wadi bed
highlights.note: The light stony strip lies at the bottom of the visible ravine. It establishes terrain context, not the location of a particular pool, water-channel junction, or Copper Scroll deposit.

title: Excavated Pool of Siloam steps
author: Ian Scott
viewpoint: At the excavated Pool of Siloam in Jerusalem, looking along the surviving stepped edge; precise camera coordinates are not supplied by the source.
alt: Ground-level photograph along several broad stone steps at the excavated Pool of Siloam, with a paved strip on the right, exposed masonry above, and a modern access stair in the distance.
caption: The larger southern stepped pool, photographed in May 2009. This lies within the broader Siloam area; it is not the smaller Silwan pool and tunnel outlet considered for entry 49. The research distinguishes the two installations and discusses the larger basin under Solomon’s Pool (Q37).

highlights.label: Surviving pool steps
highlights.note: The broad steps belong to the excavated southern pool. Entry 49’s proposed Siloam reading concerns a water installation and trough: neither the proposed trough nor the tunnel outlet is visible here. These steps supply context for the wider area only.

highlights.label: Return of the stepped edge
highlights.note: The photograph shows the steps turning at the far end of this exposed portion. Other sides of the ancient pool, its water supply outlet, and features buried beyond the excavation are not visible.
